panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Axial T1-weighted MRI demonstrates classic features of Morel-Lavallée lesion: mass overlaying fascia (fascial plane separation), internal fat components, and associated hematoma. B: Axial T2-WI MRI clearly demonstrates fluid-fluid levels within the collection, a feature described in the context of chronicity. C: Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated image confirms the suppression of the central fatty component of the lesion. D: Coronal T1-weighted image demonstrates the lesion's fascial relationship and internal composition, showing central fatty mass. E: Coronal PD fat saturation sequence demonstrates the suppressed fatty core and heterogeneous surrounding tissue. F: Coronal T1-weighted fat-saturated sequence provides another view of the suppressed central fatty mass and its heterogeneous contents.

The mass ‎appeared with two zones: a high-intensity central oval shape zone, which represents a fatty ‎mass (yellow star), and a hematoma, which displays a homogeneous hyperintense signal to skeletal muscle ‎‎(green and blue stars), surrounded by low-intensity peripheral pseudocapsule (blue arrows).‎ (B) Axial T2-WI at the same level as Figure A reveals multiple fluid-fluid levels indicating the chronicity of the ‎lesion (red arrows) ‎with no evidence of internal enhancement.‎ (C) Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated image at the same level as Figure A ‎displays the suppression of the central fatty ‎mass (yellow star) with heterogeneous hyperintense signal outer to the central mass. (E, F) Coronal proton density (PD) fat saturation (FS) and coronal T1-weighted fat-saturated image sequences at the same level as Figure A show the signal suppressed central fatty ‎mass (yellow star) with heterogeneous ‎intermediate to hyperintense signal outer to it‎, surrounded ‎with low-intensity peripheral pseudocapsule (blue arrows).‎
